chapter: Dance jobs and the opera house
title: Pay and bosses at the opera house after the Silver Slipper
summary: He compares Silver Slipper pay with the $6 scale at the opera house, recounts proving he could read, and lists the owners he played for.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Getting back to that, when I first went to the opera house, I went with, it was Paul Moyer, and the Sam Hopkins playing piano. I told him I wasn't gonna rest him for a couple of weeks, but right with the Silver Slipper, was just making so much money, just making, oh, I guess, $40, $50, $90, $90, $10. Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah. And when I went to the opera house, the scale was $6. And when I stayed there, and first night I went there, a man asked me, he said, can you read? I said, read a little. He said, I got this number, no, it was in Washington Square. He said, several bands there, he said. I don't seem to get nobody wanted to play. I said, well, if you don't, you don't own a place and want the number playing, I'll play it. So he'd give it to me, he said, you think you'll have it ready for next week's rehearsal? When I look at the thing, Rose of Washington Square, he said, anybody could play it. I guess the one who was there just didn't want to play it, see? I know good what a captain played if he wanted to play it, you know? So I said, your wife got a costume made? He said, yeah. I said, well, she can do it tonight if she wants. What do you mean? I said, that's what I said. So I went on and played Don once, and he said, well, I'll be doggone. And he'd come to me and say, your son was raised a dollar tonight. I thought nine, he said, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. So, well, I played there for him, and then when he sold the place, the Baron King, I stayed there with him. I played for Stormy. And then when she left, Dolly Faye came and played there for them. And then Nick Connell took the place. I played a while for him, then, but they had different ideas. They were my chief man, you know? So, and then that. Did anybody ever tell you about the trumpet player around him by the name of Kimball?
